PullRequest.Title: agentHost: attribute restricted engine snapshots per model call
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

## What and why

Agent Host forwards the Copilot runtime's restricted `engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length` snapshots. A conversation can switch models or run subagents on another model, so the conversation's selected model does not identify the model behind each snapshot. A Copilot runtime update will add per-call metadata to these snapshots. This change prepares the Agent Host to forward that metadata and adds the SDK version it knows itself.

- **Declares the per-call fields** the runtime attaches: `requestModel`, `responseModel`, `interactionType`, `parentToolCallId` and `runtimeVersion`. The router already passes runtime properties through unchanged, so these fields flow as soon as the runtime sends them. Older runtimes omit them, and the router leaves them absent. Model names are classified as `CustomerContent` because a bring-your-own-key model name is chosen by the user, and they stay on restricted destinations.
- **Stamps `copilotSdkVersion`**, the Copilot SDK package bundled with this Agent Host (`IProductService.copilotVersions.sdk`), on engine snapshots. Until now the SDK and runtime versions were common properties only on standard telemetry, so engine snapshots carried just the editor version. A value already present in the notification is replaced, matching how the router handles `sdkSessionId` and `sdkAgentId`. Editor version, SDK package version and runtime version stay separate fields. Native Agent Host engine events have no extension version to report.
- **Documents the field meanings** in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md`.

Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10632.

## Scope

No new event, destination, consent check or content-exclusion change. Until the SDK/runtime dependency is updated, the only addition on the wire is `copilotSdkVersion`. Backend retention of the new properties is tracked separately.

## How to test

```text
pnpm run test-node --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.test.ts
```

Result: **31 passing**. The new test routes synthetic notifications through the real restricted sender and checks the upload envelopes for three cases:

- a root call whose reported model differs from the requested one;
- a subagent call with a spawning tool call and no reported model;
- a call from an older runtime that sends none of the fields.

It also checks that an SDK version supplied in the notification is replaced, and that consent-disabled and non-restricted notifications are not uploaded.

```text
pnpm run typecheck-client
pnpm run eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.test.ts
```

Result: both **passed**.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Agent Host construction and client startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The constructor reads productService.copilotVersions.sdk once and stores it on the telemetry router. Client startup later registers a fire-and-forget telemetry callback; no changed work must complete before client.start() or user interaction can progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One router instance per CopilotAgent; the added constructor work is a single optional string property read independent of chats, model calls, or history size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work, queue, limiter, IPC, or subprocess activity is introduced during construction. Runtime telemetry callbacks remain independently fire-and-forget as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or changed by the new SDK-version constructor argument.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the constructor and client-options call path: the version is read once and only retained as a short string.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the changed startup operation is constant-time and does not add an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds constant-size router state and no startup-critical work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Routing restricted engine.messages and engine.messages.length snapshots for root calls, subagents, and older runtimes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK invokes onGitHubTelemetry via a void, fire-and-forget callback, so routing and upload are off the model-call/user-response critical path. Routing resolves the existing per-token telemetry context, multiplexes existing event properties, serializes an envelope, and starts the existing telemetry send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the restricted telemetry context through per-token Copilot account discovery on a cold cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced cold discovery for concurrent callers sharing a token; warm notifications reuse the cached entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same context resolution occurred for every targeted restricted notification before the diff, with the same per-token caching/coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by telemetry routing only; the SDK callback does not await routing, so model-call progress is not blocked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy properties, gzip/base64 values that are already oversized or always-compressed, and JSON-serialize the telemetry envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per existing routed snapshot; compression remains once per qualifying large property. copilotSdkVersion is short and does not qualify for compression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All event properties were already copied, multiplexed, and serialized. The diff adds only one short property to engine snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only on the off-critical-path telemetry route; envelope JSON serialization occurs before the fire-and-forget POST.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST one Application Insights envelope for each eligible enhanced GitHub telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing POST per eligible engine snapshot; zero when restricted telemetry is disabled. The diff adds no POST and no destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events already produced the same POST cardinality; only the serialized envelope gains a bounded SDK-version field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fetch is fire-and-forget and does not delay the model call or response path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of runtime-emitted engine snapshots, typically the existing engine.messages and engine.messages.length events per model call across root and subagent calls. The diff creates no events; it adds one bounded SDK-version string per existing snapshot. The five runtime metadata fields were already passed through by the pre-diff event.properties spread, so their client-side cardinality and serialization are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each notification is routed independently as before. Concurrent cold context lookups for the same token share the existing discovery promise; warm lookups use the cached per-token entry. Telemetry POSTs remain fire-and-forget and can overlap, but the diff neither increases event count nor changes concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold per-token restricted-context discovery may perform one coalesced /copilot_internal/user request; warm notifications reuse the cached entry. The diff does not alter cache keys, positive/negative states, coalescing, or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the pre-diff router already spread every runtime property, while the sole runtime behavior change stamps one optional short string before the existing multiplex/send path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact snapshot frequency varies with model calls and subagent fan-out, but that affects only a constant payload-byte delta because event count and boundary-call count are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added SDK-version field causes a negligible constant payload/allocation increase per pre-existing event and does not introduce fan-out, blocking, cache misses, or new boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced startup plus restricted engine telemetry through cache resolution, multiplexing, serialization, internal routing, and network upload. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
